disclaimerText: This report is research output only. Nothing in it has been validated, is executable, or carries any profitability claim. Every rule-like statement here requires replay validation and paper-trading validation before it could ever be considered for live or paper execution -- and even then, only through the existing StrategyRule promotion pipeline, never automatically from this report.

evidenceExcerpts.exactExcerpt: the london session right starts at 7 00 am gmt and

explicitRules.normalizedClaim: Session hours are given explicitly in GMT: London 07:00-16:00 and New York 12:00-21:00 during US daylight saving; London 08:00-17:00 and New York 13:00-22:00 during standard time. Four sessions are named: Sydney, Tokyo, London, New York.

evidenceExcerpts.exactExcerpt: the most volatile session right in the forex market is during the london

explicitRules.normalizedClaim: The London/New York overlap is identified as the most volatile period of the forex day, on the stated reasoning that both of the largest financial centres are open simultaneously.

evidenceExcerpts.exactExcerpt: leverage can amplify your gains and losses

explicitRules.normalizedClaim: Leverage amplifies gains and losses symmetrically. The worked example: a 1:10 leveraged position turns a 10% adverse move into a 100% loss of capital.

evidenceExcerpts.exactExcerpt: risk management is the ability as a trader to encounter a series of losses right and not

explicitRules.normalizedClaim: Risk management is defined as the ability to survive a series of consecutive losses with the account substantially intact - the worked benchmark is ten losses in a row.

evidenceExcerpts.exactExcerpt: you can have a winning trading strategy but without proper risk management right you will still end up

explicitRules.normalizedClaim: A profitable strategy without risk management is asserted to still produce a losing trader. Demonstrated with two traders on identical 50%-win, 1:2 strategies where the one risking 25% per trade is wiped out before the winning streak arrives.

evidenceExcerpts.exactExcerpt: not to lose more than one percent of your trading account on each trade

explicitRules.normalizedClaim: The stated general guideline is to risk no more than 1% of the account per trade, with 2-3% noted as a choice some traders make.

evidenceExcerpts.exactExcerpt: position size is equals to the amount to risk right the amount of uh dollar
such that we don't lose more than one percent of our current of our ac

explicitRules.normalizedClaim: Position size = amount to risk / (stop-loss distance x value per pip). A complete, mechanical sizing formula.

evidenceExcerpts.exactExcerpt: so this is what we call a one to two risk reward ratio your reward right it's two times your initial risk

explicitRules.normalizedClaim: Risk-to-reward ratio is defined as reward as a multiple of the amount risked, worked through at 1:2 and 1:10.

evidenceExcerpts.exactExcerpt: a stop loss order is in order to sell your position if the price

explicitRules.normalizedClaim: A stop-loss order exits the position when price reaches a specified level against the trade. It is the only one of the four order types whose function is exiting rather than entering.

evidenceExcerpts.exactExcerpt: as a trader who uses leverage in your trading i still suggest you use a stop-loss order

explicitRules.normalizedClaim: A stop-loss is recommended on every trade for a leveraged trader, with the acknowledged cost that it will sometimes stop a trade out prematurely.

evidenceExcerpts.exactExcerpt: for a buy limit order right it's an order an order to buy below the current market price

explicitRules.normalizedClaim: A buy limit order enters below the current market price and fills only if price reaches that level; the acknowledged cost is that it may never fill.

evidenceExcerpts.exactExcerpt: the higher the spread the higher your transaction cost

explicitRules.normalizedClaim: The spread is the transaction cost in forex, where commission is usually not charged. Worked: one standard lot of EURUSD at a 3-pip spread costs $30 on entry.

evidenceExcerpts.exactExcerpt: if you trade off the higher time frame your stop-loss is usually wider

explicitRules.normalizedClaim: Spread cost should be assessed as a percentage of stop-loss distance, not in absolute pips. A 1-pip spread is 20% of a 5-pip stop but 1% of a 100-pip stop, which is given as a reason to prefer higher timeframes.

evidenceExcerpts.exactExcerpt: an uptrend consists of a series of higher highs and higher low

explicitRules.normalizedClaim: An uptrend is a series of higher highs and higher lows.

evidenceExcerpts.exactExcerpt: downtrend right in essence is a series of lower highs and lower low

explicitRules.normalizedClaim: A downtrend is a series of lower highs and lower lows.

evidenceExcerpts.exactExcerpt: price is contained between the highs and the lows

explicitRules.normalizedClaim: A range is price contained between highs and lows, distinguished from a trend by repeated rejection at the boundary rather than a break beyond it. In a range both directions are tradeable.

evidenceExcerpts.exactExcerpt: market structure helps you to define the current market condition
what is the market structure this would

explicitRules.normalizedClaim: Market structure is the first question to answer on any chart - buy, sell, or stay out - and everything else is secondary to it.

evidenceExcerpts.exactExcerpt: for you the beginner is much easier to be trading along the path of least resistance

explicitRules.normalizedClaim: Trade in the direction of the trend. Counter-trend trading is acknowledged as a valid specialisation for some traders, but is not recommended for beginners.

evidenceExcerpts.exactExcerpt: pay attention to the swing points the ones that really

explicitRules.normalizedClaim: Only major swing points - those that visibly stand out - are used to identify structure. Minor highs and lows are deliberately ignored on the stated reasoning that including them loses the larger picture.

evidenceExcerpts.exactExcerpt: look from left to right left to right don't just look at the

explicitRules.normalizedClaim: Structure is read across the whole visible chart from left to right rather than from the most recent few candles.

evidenceExcerpts.exactExcerpt: when you deal with technical analysis there is subjectivity involved

explicitRules.normalizedClaim: Structure classification is stated to be subjective: a chart he calls a range may reasonably be called an uptrend by another trader, and neither is declared wrong.

evidenceExcerpts.exactExcerpt: if it's not clear if it's conflicting information move on onto another currency pair

explicitRules.normalizedClaim: When a chart is ambiguous the prescribed action is to skip it and look at another instrument. Staying out is treated as a valid decision rather than a failure to decide.

evidenceExcerpts.exactExcerpt: it tells you where to buy or sell the key word here is where

explicitRules.normalizedClaim: Area of value answers WHERE to trade, as distinct from market structure which answers WHAT to do. Being in a trend is explicitly not a reason to enter.

evidenceExcerpts.exactExcerpt: support is an area on your chart where buying pressure could step in

explicitRules.normalizedClaim: Support is an area where buying pressure COULD step in; resistance is an area where selling pressure COULD step in. The conditional is stated deliberately - trading is described as probabilities, never certainty.

evidenceExcerpts.exactExcerpt: when support is broken it tends to become or it could become resistance

explicitRules.normalizedClaim: Broken support tends to become resistance and broken resistance tends to become support.

evidenceExcerpts.exactExcerpt: support resistance they are an area on your chart

explicitRules.normalizedClaim: Support and resistance are areas rather than exact prices. Price may overshoot, undershoot or fail to touch the level before reversing, and the level must be adjusted over time as new price action arrives.

evidenceExcerpts.exactExcerpt: i use support resistance and moving average often

explicitRules.normalizedClaim: Two tools are used to locate areas of value: support/resistance and moving averages.

evidenceExcerpts.exactExcerpt: entry trigger this tells you when to buy or sell

explicitRules.normalizedClaim: The entry trigger answers WHEN to enter, completing a three-part framework: structure (what), area of value (where), entry trigger (when).

evidenceExcerpts.exactExcerpt: there is four data points for every candlestick pattern you have the opening price the closing

explicitRules.normalizedClaim: Every candle carries four data points - open, close, high and low of the session - and the body/wick terminology follows from them.

evidenceExcerpts.exactExcerpt: the technicians call it a hammer

explicitRules.normalizedClaim: The hammer: sellers push price to the lows of the session, buyers reclaim it and close near the highs. Read as buyers taking control.

evidenceExcerpts.exactExcerpt: it opened low and closed even higher than the previous day opening price

explicitRules.normalizedClaim: Bullish engulfing: a down candle followed by an up candle that opens lower and closes beyond the prior candle's opening price, read as buyers overwhelming the prior session's sellers. The bearish version is the inverse.

evidenceExcerpts.exactExcerpt: most of these patterns are pretty much a variation of one another

explicitRules.normalizedClaim: Memorising the full catalogue of candlestick names is described as unnecessary because the patterns are variations on the same idea; what matters is reading who ended the session in control.

evidenceExcerpts.exactExcerpt: the market structure is in the downtrend area of value the price is at resistance our entry trigger we have a bearish engulfing pattern

explicitRules.normalizedClaim: A valid setup requires all three components to align: structure, area of value, and entry trigger. Demonstrated on USDZAR - downtrend, price at resistance, bearish engulfing.

evidenceExcerpts.exactExcerpt: this is clearly a cherry pick chart

explicitRules.normalizedClaim: The teaching examples are explicitly acknowledged as cherry-picked, and the source states that real trading will not look this clean.

evidenceExcerpts.exactExcerpt: want to set your stop-loss at a level which invalidates your trading setup

explicitRules.normalizedClaim: The stop is placed at the level that would invalidate the trade's premise - for a buy-at-support setup, below the support area, because a break there falsifies the hypothesis the trade was based on.

evidenceExcerpts.exactExcerpt: you can use an indicator called the average true range
so what i'm gonna do is take seven two dot seven two

explicitRules.normalizedClaim: The stop distance is set objectively as: the low of the support area minus one ATR. The stated ATR setting is a 20-period ATR using SMA.

evidenceExcerpts.exactExcerpt: we don't just want to set it smack below support because

explicitRules.normalizedClaim: The stop is deliberately NOT placed immediately below support, on the stated reasoning that price frequently spikes just beyond the level before continuing. The ATR buffer exists to absorb that.

evidenceExcerpts.exactExcerpt: i call this uh stack areas because you have multiple factors coming together

explicitRules.normalizedClaim: Where two independent areas of value coincide - here a 50-period moving average and a prior resistance-turned-support - the confluence is named a 'stacked area' and treated as stronger than either alone.

evidenceExcerpts.exactExcerpt: we usually want to set our target profit at before right previous swing highs are low in the market
you're making difficult for the market you know to give you a profit so be reasonable

explicitRules.normalizedClaim: The target is set just BEFORE the nearest opposing swing high or low, not at it, because that level is where opposing pressure is expected and because the level is an area rather than a price.

evidenceExcerpts.exactExcerpt: what you can do is to use a buy limit order

explicitRules.normalizedClaim: When risk-to-reward is unattractive, the prescribed fix is to improve the ENTRY using a buy limit order, not to move the stop.

evidenceExcerpts.exactExcerpt: we don't want to mess with our stop-loss because our stop-loss is at a

explicitRules.normalizedClaim: The stop must not be tightened to improve risk-to-reward, because it is placed where the setup is invalidated and exiting before that point is not coherent with the trade's premise.

evidenceExcerpts.exactExcerpt: don't set your target above the highs of this resistance because you are expecting the price to break above that resistance

explicitRules.normalizedClaim: The target must not be moved beyond an opposing level merely to make risk-to-reward look acceptable. In a range this is called a very bad idea; in a trend, extending the target past a prior swing high is described as a defensible but lower-probability choice.

evidenceExcerpts.exactExcerpt: i want to show you how a losing trade looks like

explicitRules.normalizedClaim: A losing trade is shown deliberately: a setup meeting all three criteria with a correctly-placed stop is stopped out, and price then rallies. Stated to be a trade he took himself.

evidenceExcerpts.exactExcerpt: no matter how good a trading setup looks like no

explicitRules.normalizedClaim: A correct setup with a correctly-placed stop will still lose, sometimes immediately before the move it predicted. Presented as a permanent feature of trading rather than an error to be engineered away.

evidenceExcerpts.exactExcerpt: it's not near any area of value

explicitRules.normalizedClaim: A trade with correct structure but no area of value is skipped. Demonstrated twice - including one case with a valid entry trigger present, which is still skipped because the area of value is missing.

evidenceExcerpts.exactExcerpt: if it's not at an area of value then really usually i don't even bother looking at the entry trigger

explicitRules.normalizedClaim: The three components are ordered and gated: without an area of value the entry trigger is not even evaluated.

preferredConditions.statement: A buy limit order enters below the current market price and fills only if price reaches that level; the acknowledged cost is that it may never fill.
Trade in the direction of the trend. Counter-trend trading is acknowledged as a valid specialisation for some traders, but is not recommended for beginners.
Area of value answers WHERE to trade, as distinct from market structure which answers WHAT to do. Being in a trend is explicitly not a reason to enter.
Two tools are used to locate areas of value: support/resistance and moving averages.
When risk-to-reward is unattractive, the prescribed fix is to improve the ENTRY using a buy limit order, not to move the stop.
Market structure is the first question to answer on any chart - buy, sell, or stay out - and everything else is secondary to it.

Only major swing points - those that visibly stand out - are used to identify structure. Minor highs and lows are deliberately ignored on the stated reasoning that including them loses the larger picture.
Structure is read across the whole visible chart from left to right rather than from the most recent few candles.
A valid setup requires all three components to align: structure, area of value, and entry trigger. Demonstrated on USDZAR - downtrend, price at resistance, bearish engulfing.

Where two independent areas of value coincide - here a 50-period moving average and a prior resistance-turned-support - the confluence is named a 'stacked area' and treated as stronger than either alone.
The three components are ordered and gated: without an area of value the entry trigger is not even evaluated.
The entry trigger answers WHEN to enter, completing a three-part framework: structure (what), area of value (where), entry trigger (when).
The hammer: sellers push price to the lows of the session, buyers reclaim it and close near the highs. Read as buyers taking control.

Bullish engulfing: a down candle followed by an up candle that opens lower and closes beyond the prior candle's opening price, read as buyers overwhelming the prior session's sellers. The bearish version is the inverse.

profitTargets.statement: The target is set just BEFORE the nearest opposing swing high or low, not at it, because that level is where opposing pressure is expected and because the level is an area rather than a price.

The target must not be moved beyond an opposing level merely to make risk-to-reward look acceptable. In a range this is called a very bad idea; in a trend, extending the target past a prior swing high is described as a defensible but lower-probability choice.

setupInvalidation.statement: When a chart is ambiguous the prescribed action is to skip it and look at another instrument. Staying out is treated as a valid decision rather than a failure to decide.

A trade with correct structure but no area of value is skipped. Demonstrated twice - including one case with a valid entry trigger present, which is still skipped because the area of value is missing.

stopPlacement.statement: A stop-loss order exits the position when price reaches a specified level against the trade. It is the only one of the four order types whose function is exiting rather than entering.
A stop-loss is recommended on every trade for a leveraged trader, with the acknowledged cost that it will sometimes stop a trade out prematurely.
The stop is placed at the level that would invalidate the trade's premise - for a buy-at-support setup, below the support area, because a break there falsifies the hypothesis the trade was based on.
The stop distance is set objectively as: the low of the support area minus one ATR. The stated ATR setting is a 20-period ATR using SMA.
The stop is deliberately NOT placed immediately below support, on the stated reasoning that price frequently spikes just beyond the level before continuing. The ATR buffer exists to absorb that.
The stop must not be tightened to improve risk-to-reward, because it is placed where the setup is invalidated and exiting before that point is not coherent with the trade's premise.

primaryConcepts.value: Market structure is the first question to answer on any chart - buy, sell, or stay out - and everything else is secondary to it.

The three components are ordered and gated: without an area of value the entry trigger is not even evaluated.
Risk-to-reward ratio is defined as reward as a multiple of the amount risked, worked through at 1:2 and 1:10.
An uptrend is a series of higher highs and higher lows.
A downtrend is a series of lower highs and lower lows.
A range is price contained between highs and lows, distinguished from a trend by repeated rejection at the boundary rather than a break beyond it. In a range both directions are tradeable.

Support is an area where buying pressure COULD step in; resistance is an area where selling pressure COULD step in. The conditional is stated deliberately - trading is described as probabilities, never certainty.
Broken support tends to become resistance and broken resistance tends to become support.

Support and resistance are areas rather than exact prices. Price may overshoot, undershoot or fail to touch the level before reversing, and the level must be adjusted over time as new price action arrives.
Every candle carries four data points - open, close, high and low of the session - and the body/wick terminology follows from them.
